scope: DSCG third-layer options, research-only; targeted literature investigation, not exhaustive systematic review
notes: No source ASR is treated as DSCG efficacy.
Read versions are explicit and may differ from a later version.
No full copyrighted paper text is stored; findings are paraphrased.
Bibliographic and claim checks are research notes, not independent reproductions.

sources.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
sources.read_locations: Evaluation design, attack/defense setup; official metadata
sources.claim_support: Dynamic task environment measures utility and security; native failures also occur without attack.
sources.limitations: Native predicates are not a universal independent injection oracle.
sources.verification_method: Primary paper/official venue page through web tool; cited methods and counterexamples inspected.

sources.title: Defending Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks With Spotlighting
sources.claim_support: Source marking separates untrusted data from instructions without training.
sources.limitations: Prompt-based trust boundaries do not create object permissions or hard enforcement.
sources.verification_method: Primary paper/official venue page through web tool; cited methods and counterexamples inspected.

sources.title: StruQ: Defending Against Prompt Injection with Structured Queries
sources.read_locations: Secure frontend and structured instruction tuning; official metadata
sources.claim_support: The method combines a secure frontend with a specially trained model.
sources.limitations: A JSON wrapper with an unchanged API model is not a reproduction of StruQ.
sources.verification_method: Primary paper/official venue page through web tool; cited methods and counterexamples inspected.

sources.title: PromptArmor: Simple yet Effective Prompt Injection Defenses
sources.claim_support: Off-the-shelf LLM detection followed by extraction and fuzzy deletion before backend processing.
sources.limitations: Our proposed one-call exact-span deletion is a variant, not the paper method; no generic guarantee.
sources.verification_method: Primary paper/official venue page through web tool; cited methods and counterexamples inspected.

sources.title: Defending Against Prompt Injection with DataFilter
sources.read_locations: Training/method, V-G Table VIII, V-H, Appendix C
sources.claim_support: Task-conditioned trained filtering; false negatives for task-consistent billing and false positives for recipe instructions. Table VIII reports PromptArmor 93% and DataFilter 83% ASR under its strong adaptive experiment.
sources.limitations: These are DataFilter authors' comparison results, not direct Nasr results or DSCG rates; cost/latency figures are estimates.
sources.verification_method: Primary paper/official venue page through web tool; cited methods and counterexamples inspected.

sources.title: The Task Shield: Enforcing Task Alignment to Defend Against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
sources.read_locations: Task extraction, contributes-to check, tool-call check and unfinished-task feedback/Figure 7
sources.claim_support: Task alignment checks and completion reminders are close prior mechanisms.
sources.limitations: A second task-necessity judge or ordinary completion feedback is not an independent new layer.
sources.verification_method: Primary paper/official venue page through web tool; cited methods and counterexamples inspected.

sources.title: τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
sources.publication_status: arXiv preprint; no later venue asserted
sources.read_locations: Abstract/evaluation method; official envs/base.py reward calculation
sources.claim_support: Annotated goal database states and required-output checks evaluate completion.
sources.limitations: Evaluator-only truth is not deployable agent context; substring checks do not establish semantic accuracy.
sources.verification_method: Primary paper/official venue page through web tool; cited methods and counterexamples inspected.

sources.title: Defeating Prompt Injections by Design
sources.claim_support: Privileged planning, quarantined extraction, interpreter and capability policies; isolated extraction can return attacker-specified targets.
sources.limitations: Larger architectural change adjacent to the closed data-flow route; not selected for implementation.
sources.verification_method: Primary paper/official venue page through web tool; cited methods and counterexamples inspected.

sources.title: Adaptive Attacks Break Defenses Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM Agents
sources.read_locations: Threat model, eight-defense adaptive evaluation; official metadata
sources.claim_support: Defense-specific adaptive attacks bypass evaluated defenses.
sources.limitations: The evaluated defenses/models are different; no DSCG rate can be inferred.
sources.verification_method: Primary paper/official venue page through web tool; cited methods and counterexamples inspected.

sources.title: The Attacker Moves Second: Stronger Adaptive Attacks Bypass Defenses Against Llm Jailbreaks and Prompt Injections
sources.read_locations: Abstract, adaptive attack setup and Spotlighting experiment
sources.claim_support: Larger defense-aware search budgets strengthen jailbreak and prompt-injection attacks.
sources.limitations: Mixed attack domains and budgets; PromptArmor/DataFilter 93/83 figures are not attributed directly to this paper.
sources.verification_method: Primary paper/official venue page through web tool; cited methods and counterexamples inspected.

sources.title: AutoDojo: A Generative Benchmark for Evaluating Prompt Injection Defenses in LLM Agents

sources.claim_support: Black-box adaptive injections on AgentDojo/AgentDyn; task specification influences vulnerability.
sources.limitations: Use the v3 title, not the earlier v1 title; not implemented or run in DSCG.
